blocks.text: MRI is a high-yield paediatric investigation station, particularly for **neurology, developmental abnormalities, seizures, spinal disease, tumours, musculoskeletal pathology and congenital abnormalities**.
Unlike CT, MRI does **not use ionising radiation** and provides excellent soft-tissue contrast.
For the OSCE, your goal is not to memorise every MRI sequence. You need to be able to:

subsections.subsection_title: 35. CT VS MRI — EXAMINER'S FAVOURITE QUESTION

blocks.text: **“A child has suffered a significant head injury. Why might you choose CT rather than MRI initially?”**

“CT is rapid, widely available in emergency settings and excellent for detecting acute intracranial haemorrhage and skull fractures. In an unstable trauma patient, speed is particularly important. MRI may subsequently provide more detailed assessment of brain parenchymal and soft-tissue injury.”
